title: The Gods Consider Odysseus
script: Book one. Athena Inspires the Prince. Scene one. The Gods Consider Odysseus.
The gods take their places in a widening ring. Poseidon’s seat remains empty.
Mortals are quick to blame the gods, yet they heap fresh grief upon the portion fate has given them. Aegisthus was warned; he chose the act and paid its price.
Then turn your eyes from the man who earned his death to the man who still endures. Odysseus wastes on Calypso’s island, longing for the smoke of home.
Poseidon’s anger bars the road, but one god cannot stand forever against the purpose of us all. Set the return in motion.

title: Athena's Two-Part Plan
script: Hermes, carry our decree to Ogygia: Calypso must release Odysseus and let the exile begin his voyage home.
I will go to Ithaca. The father needs a road home; the son needs the courage to open it.
So the gods split the work of return: one command would free the father, another would awaken the son.
Athena fastens the gold sandals, closes her hand around the spear, and drops from Olympus.

title: The Stranger at the Threshold
script: Scene three. The Stranger at the Threshold.
Wearing the shape of Mentes, Athena waits at the palace threshold with her spear upright.
Dice strike the floor; cups are filled; the suitors never look toward the gate.
Telemachus sees the unattended stranger and crosses the hall, ashamed of his own house.
Welcome, stranger. Eat with us first; when you are rested, tell me what brought you here.

title: Mentes Questions the Prince
script: Scene four. Mentes Questions the Prince.
Telemachus gives the stranger the chair of honor and sits close enough to keep the conversation private.
They sing over another man’s stores as though the house were theirs. My father is called dead, and they are eating the proof of his life piece by piece.
I am Mentes of Taphos, an old guest-friend of your father’s house. And hear this: Odysseus is alive. He is held back, not buried.
You carry too much of Odysseus in your face for this ruin to be natural. Why do these men command your hall?

title: Athena Arms Telemachus with a Course
script: Scene five. Athena Arms Telemachus with a Course.
My mother will neither choose a husband nor end their waiting, and they punish the delay by stripping our house. Soon there will be nothing left for me to inherit but their contempt.
If Odysseus crossed that threshold with shield and spear, these men would learn how brief a wedding feast can be. Their conduct is an insult crying out for an answer.
At dawn, call the island to assembly. Order the suitors out. Then fit a ship, sail to Pylos and Sparta, and bring back the truth about your father.
Remember Orestes: he made a name by answering the injury done to his father. You cannot remain a boy while other men consume your house.

title: The Goddess Departs; the Prince Speaks
script: Scene six. The Goddess Departs; the Prince Speaks.
Keep the gift until I return. What matters now is not what you give me, but what you do when morning comes.
The goddess rises like a bird; Telemachus returns to the hall with his posture changed.
Phemius, enough. Choose another song, one that does not drag my husband through this house as though loss were entertainment.
Mother, let the singer choose his song. Return to your work; at dawn I will call the men of Ithaca to assembly, and this house will hear my command.
Night sealed the household, but Telemachus lay awake inside the course Athena had set.

title: Telemachus Calls the Assembly
script: Book two. Telemachus Sets Sail. Scene one. Telemachus Calls the Assembly.
Call every man to the meeting ground. The house of Odysseus will be silent no longer.
He enters with two hounds and takes the seat that belonged to his father.
Who has called us here, the young or the old? What danger has broken the silence of twenty years?
I called you. I have lost my father, and now men born among you are destroying his house while you watch.

title: The Secret of Penelope's Loom
script: Scene two. The Secret of Penelope's Loom.
Do not blame the suitors for your mother’s cunning. Penelope keeps every man waiting and makes promises she will not finish.
For three years she wove Laertes’ shroud by daylight and pulled it apart by torchlight. She made time itself her accomplice.
A maid betrayed the trick. We caught her at the loom and forced the web to its end.
Send her to her father. Let Icarius arrange the marriage, and this house will be free of us.

title: The Eagles Tear the Air
script: Scene three. The Eagles Tear the Air.
I will not drive my mother from the house that is hers. Leave my halls and feast on your own goods, or answer to the gods for what you consume here.
Two eagles descend, wheel over the assembly, and tear at one another before vanishing inland.
Odysseus is near. The eagles have shown blood within the house, and the men who mock his return are standing inside the omen.
Go home and read signs for your own children, old man. No bird will bring Odysseus back, and your prophecy will not frighten us from this feast.

title: Mentor Rebukes Ithaca
script: Hear me plainly. Announces a voyage to Pylos and Sparta for news of Odysseus.
This cannot stand: the people for forgetting the king and tolerating the suitors.
Let all of you remember this: that even Odysseus could not defeat the suitors now gathered.
Citizens disperse and the suitors return to the palace.

title: Athena Answers on the Shore
script: Scene five. Athena Answers on the Shore.
I promise: he will not lack courage.
See the matter clearly. Gather provisions while you recruits a crew and finds a ship.
The voyage becomes a hidden operation running beneath the suitors' gaze.

title: The Secret Stores
script: No. I will not Antinous's false friendliness.
Telemachus enters the locked storeroom filled with metal, cloth, oil, wine, and meal.
Prepare twelve jars of wine and twenty measures of barley.
I swear: protests in fear, then swears not to tell Penelope.

title: The Night Launch
script: Athena, disguised as Telemachus, recruits crewmen and borrows Noemon's ship.
The crew carries provisions from the palace and stows them below deck.
Athena takes the pilot's seat and sends a strong west wind.
The sail fills, libations are poured, and the ship travels through the night.

title: Arrival at Poseidon's Sacrifice
script: Book three. King Nestor Remembers. Scene one. Arrival at Poseidon's Sacrifice.
At sunrise the ship reaches Pylos, where nine great divisions sacrifice black bulls to Poseidon.
Take the next step: Him past your shyness.
Welcome. Come inside, take food, and speak when you are ready.
Hear me, Poseidon and passes the cup to Telemachus.

title: Telemachus Questions Nestor
script: Who you are and whether you are traders or raiders?
For the unsoftened truth about Odysseus?
Nestor begins the account of the quarrel that split the returning Greek fleet.

title: The Broken Return from Troy
script: Scene three. The Broken Return from Troy.
Listen, and I will tell it in order. the feud between Agamemnon and Menelaus after Troy fell.
Odysseus turned back to support Agamemnon.
Nestor, Diomedes, and Menelaus escaped by a difficult route and reached home.
Admits he learned Odysseus's later fate only through scattered reports.

title: Orestes as the Measure
script: Scene four. Orestes as the Measure.
Tells how Aegisthus murdered Agamemnon and how Orestes later took revenge.
Become a son whose deed will be sung.
Telemachus wishes for the power to punish the suitors but doubts the gods will grant it.
Rebukes his despair and insists a willing god can save a mortal.

title: Athena Reveals Herself at Pylos
script: Scene five. Athena Reveals Herself at Pylos.
Night approaches and Nestor invites the guests to his palace.
No. I will not and suddenly flies away in the form of a sea-eagle.
At dawn a heifer is sacrificed.
Telemachus is bathed and dressed for departure.

title: The Chariot Road to Sparta
script: Scene six. The Chariot Road to Sparta.
Horses harnessed and provisions loaded for you.
Pisistratus takes the reins beside him and drives out of Pylos.
Pisistratus spend the night at Phera under Diocles's hospitality.
At dawn they continue through wheatlands toward Lacedaemon.

bookTitle: The King and Queen of Sparta
title: The Double Wedding at Sparta
script: Book four. The King and Queen of Sparta. Scene one. The Double Wedding at Sparta.
Telemachus and Pisistratus reach Menelaus's palace during a double wedding feast.
Attendants unharness the horses, bathe the guests, and seat them at the feast.
Marvels at the palace's brilliance while Menelaus speaks of the grief beneath wealth.

bookTitle: The King and Queen of Sparta
title: Recognition through Tears
script: Speaks of Odysseus and Telemachus hides his tears behind his cloak.
Enters, recognizes Telemachus by resemblance, and names him aloud.
Pisistratus confirms the identity and recalls his own dead brother Antilochus.
Come, for the mourning to end with the meal.

bookTitle: The King and Queen of Sparta
title: Helen's Drug and the Beggar in Troy
script: Scene three. Helen's Drug and the Beggar in Troy.
Helen mixes a drug into the wine that quiets grief and anger.
Tells how Odysseus entered Troy disguised as a beaten slave.
Helen alone recognized and bathed him.
he revealed the Greek plan after binding her to secrecy.
Odysseus killed Trojans and returned to the ships with intelligence.

bookTitle: The King and Queen of Sparta
title: The Wooden Horse
script: With the story of the wooden horse.
Helen circled the horse and imitated the voices of the warriors' wives.
Odysseus restrained them and silenced Anticlus.
Telemachus hears proof of his father's endurance and command under pressure.

bookTitle: The King and Queen of Sparta
title: Menelaus Wrestles Proteus
script: Listen, and I will tell it in order. being trapped in Egypt until Eidothea taught him to seize Proteus.
Menelaus and three men hid beneath sealskins and grappled the Old Man of the Sea.
Proteus changed into beasts, water, and a tree before yielding prophecy.
Proteus revealed that Odysseus lived, detained by Calypso on an island.

bookTitle: The King and Queen of Sparta
title: The Gifts and the Eagle Omen
script: Scene six. The Gifts and the Eagle Omen.
The king exchanges the offered horses for a mixing bowl suited to rocky Ithaca.
Gives Telemachus a robe for his future bride.
As the travelers depart, an eagle carrying a goose appears and Helen reads it as Odysseus's returning vengeance.

bookTitle: The King and Queen of Sparta
title: The Suitors Prepare an Ambush
script: Scene seven. The Suitors Prepare an Ambush.
When Telemachus will return your ship?
The suitors discover that the voyage truly occurred without their knowledge.
Antinous selects a crew and sails to the strait between Ithaca and Same to ambush the prince.
Athena sends a phantom in the shape of Iphthime to reassure the sleeping queen.

title: Hermes Carries the Decree
script: Book five. Odysseus—Nymph and Shipwreck. Scene one. Hermes Carries the Decree.
The gods meet again and Athena presses the case of Odysseus and Telemachus.
Tell Calypso that Odysseus must depart without divine escort.
Hermes straps on his sandals, takes his wand, and skims across the sea.
Hermes reaches Ogygia, enters Calypso's fragrant cavern, and finds her weaving at the fire.

title: Calypso Receives the Order
script: Scene two. Calypso Receives the Order.
Take warning: her against divine anger.
Calypso denounces the gods' jealousy toward goddesses who love mortal men.
Agrees to release Odysseus but says she cannot escort him herself.

title: Odysseus Distrusts Freedom
script: Calypso suspects a trap and demands a binding oath that she will not plan his ruin.
I swear: swears by earth, sky, and Styx and offers practical help.
No. I will not he comparison's consequence.

title: Building the Raft
script: Leads Odysseus to tall trees and gives him axe, adze, augers, cloth, and cord.
Calypso fells, trims, bores, joins, decks, and fences the timbers over four days.
Calypso rigs mast, yard, sail, steering oar, and ballast.
Calypso bathes and clothes him, loads food and water, and sends a warm wind behind the raft.

title: Poseidon Breaks the Sea
script: Scene five. Poseidon Breaks the Sea.
For seventeen days Odysseus steers by the stars until Scheria rises ahead.
Poseidon sees him, gathers clouds, and strikes the sea with a four-wind storm.
Odysseus is swept away and barely regains it.
Athena restrains the winds except the north wind that drives him shoreward.

title: The River Accepts the Castaway
script: Scene six. The River Accepts the Castaway.
Odysseus swims for two nights and days while waves hurl him toward a reef-lined coast.
Athena shows him a river mouth free of rocks and wind.
Hear me, the river god, who stills the current and receives him.
Odysseus returns Ino's veil to the sea, crawls ashore, and hides beneath two intertwined olive bushes.
Odysseus buries himself in leaves and Athena seals him in sleep.

title: Athena Enters Nausicaa's Dream
script: Book six. The Princess and the Stranger. Scene one. Athena Enters Nausicaa's Dream.
Athena reaches the palace of Alcinous and enters Nausicaa's chamber in the likeness of a friend.
Athena reproaches the princess for leaving fine clothes unwashed before marriage.
Your father for a wagon, and conceals the marriage motive?
Her mother packs food, wine, and oil.

title: Laundry and Ball at the River
script: Scene two. Laundry and Ball at the River.
Nausicaa and her maids drive to the washing pools, unharness the mules, and tread the clothes clean.
Nausicaa spread garments on the shore, bathe, eat, and play ball while the clothes dry.
Athena deflects the ball into deep water.
The shout wakes Odysseus beneath the leaves.

title: The Naked Stranger Emerges
script: Scene three. The Naked Stranger Emerges.
Odysseus debates whether to clasp Nausicaa's knees or speak from a distance.
Covering himself with a leafy branch, he emerges like a mountain lion.
The maids flee, but Athena keeps Nausicaa steady.
For clothing and directions, and avoids touching your?
With courage and assigns the maids to help him.

title: Bath, Clothing, and the Road to Town
script: Scene four. Bath, Clothing, and the Road to Town.
The maids place food, oil, and clothing beside the river and withdraw while Odysseus washes.
Athena makes him appear taller, stronger, and more radiant.
Nausicaa eats while the women fold and load the dry clothes.
How to follow at a distance, wait in Athena's grove, and supplicate Queen Arete first.

title: Athena Hides the Walk through Scheria
script: Book seven. Phaeacia's Halls and Gardens. Scene one. Athena Hides the Walk through Scheria.
Nausicaa reaches the palace while Odysseus waits in Athena's grove.
Nausicaa enters the city wrapped in a divine mist.
Athena appears as a young girl carrying a pitcher and guides him through streets and harbor.
Listen closely. Question passersby, and directs him to Arete.

title: The Palace and the Gardens
script: Scene two. The Palace and the Gardens.
Odysseus stops before Alcinous's palace, dazzled by bronze walls, golden doors, and guardian dogs.
Odysseus observes the fifty women weaving and grinding within.
Outside, an orchard and garden bear fruit through every season.
Odysseus crosses the threshold under mist and finds the royal feast in progress.

title: Supplication at Arete's Knees
script: Scene three. Supplication at Arete's Knees.
Athena's mist falls away only when Odysseus reaches Arete.
Passage home, then sits humbly in the ashes by the hearth?
Odysseus is seated beside the king, fed, and promised a convoy home.

title: Arete Recognizes Her Work
script: Scene four. Arete Recognizes Her Work.
After the Phaeacians leave, Arete recognizes the clothes Odysseus wears as garments from her household.
Honor his restraint, offers marriage, and renews the promise of safe passage at dawn.

bookTitle: A Day for Songs and Contests
title: The Phaeacian Assembly and the Ship
script: Book eight. A Day for Songs and Contests. Scene one. The Phaeacian Assembly and the Ship.
At dawn Athena moves through the city in a herald's form, calling the people to assembly.
Athena makes Odysseus appear larger and more impressive as he enters.
Prepare a ship and invites the nobles to feast.
The people ready the vessel while the palace fills for celebration.

bookTitle: A Day for Songs and Contests
title: Demodocus Sings of the Quarrel
script: Scene two. Demodocus Sings of the Quarrel.
Sing now: of a quarrel between Odysseus and Achilles.
Odysseus repeatedly hides his face in his cloak and weeps.
Alcinous alone notices and stops the song by proposing athletic games.
The company moves from the hall to the contest field.

bookTitle: A Day for Songs and Contests
title: The Athletic Challenge
script: Phaeacian youths compete in running, wrestling, jumping, discus, and boxing.
Euryalus insults him as a merchant without athletic skill.
Alcinous calms the confrontation and shifts the display toward dance and song.

bookTitle: A Day for Songs and Contests
title: The Dance and the Net of Hephaestus
script: Scene four. The Dance and the Net of Hephaestus.
Sing now: how Ares and Aphrodite were trapped in Hephaestus's invisible net.
Phaeacian dancers perform a ball dance with precise leaps and exchanges.
Apologizes and gives a bronze sword.

bookTitle: A Day for Songs and Contests
title: The Trojan Horse Song and the Name
script: Scene five. The Trojan Horse Song and the Name.
For the song of the wooden horse?
Sing now: the Greeks' emergence, the sack, and Odysseus's attack on Deiphobus's house.
Odysseus weeps like a captive woman over a fallen husband.
The stranger for your name, homeland, and reason for grief?
Odysseus prepares to narrate his wanderings.

title: Odysseus Names Himself
script: Book nine. In the One-Eyed Giant's Cave. Scene one. Odysseus Names Himself.
Honor Demodocus and the ordered feast.
His name, lineage, and Ithacan homeland.
Odysseus describes Ithaca's rugged beauty and his longing to return.
Odysseus begins the account of the disasters that followed Troy.

title: The Raid on the Cicones
script: Scene two. The Raid on the Cicones.
Odysseus's fleet sacks Ismarus and divides the captured wealth.
Feast on sheep, cattle, and wine.
Cicones from inland arrive in organized force and fight through the day.
Six men from every ship are killed before the fleet escapes at dusk.

title: The Lotus-Eaters
script: A north wind drives the ships off course for nine days.
They land among the Lotus-eaters and send three scouts inland.
Those who taste it lose all desire for home.

title: Goat Island and the Cyclops Coast
script: Scene four. Goat Island and the Cyclops Coast.
The fleet reaches a fertile unworked island opposite the Cyclopes' land.
In darkness the ships enter a sheltered harbor and rest.
At dawn the crews hunt wild goats and feast while observing smoke and voices across the channel.
Odysseus takes one ship and selects twelve men to investigate the neighboring people.

title: The Empty Cave
script: Odysseus carries a skin of Maron's powerful wine and leads twelve men to a huge cave.
Odysseus find cheeses, pails, whey, lambs, and kids arranged by age.
By whatever you hold sacred, hear me: to steal food and animals and escape.
No. I will not because he wants to meet the owner and receive a guest-gift.

title: Polyphemus Seals the Cave
script: Scene six. Polyphemus Seals the Cave.
At dusk Polyphemus returns carrying a massive load of wood and drives his flock inside.
Polyphemus lifts a stone slab that no ordinary team could move and blocks the entrance.
Polyphemus milks ewes and goats, sets young beneath mothers, curdles milk, and lights a fire.
The hidden men and the giant demands their identity.

title: The First Killings
script: Come near and hear me, Zeus's protection of strangers.
Is that the best you can offer, the gods and demands to know where the ship is?
Odysseus lies that Poseidon smashed it against the rocks.
The Cyclops seizes two men, smashes them on the floor, and devours them raw.
Odysseus drinks milk and sleeps among his animals while the survivors pray in horror.

title: The Name Nobody and the Stake
script: Scene eight. The Name Nobody and the Stake.
Odysseus considers killing the sleeping giant but realizes the entrance stone would trap them forever.
At dawn Polyphemus eats two more men and leaves with the flock, sealing the cave again.
Odysseus selects a green olive trunk, cuts and smooths it into a stake, and hardens its point in the fire.
The men hide the stake beneath dung and draw lots for four helpers.
When the giant returns, I offers the potent wine and says his name is Nobody.

title: The Blinding
script: I promise: Nobody the last death as a guest-gift, and collapses.
Odysseus heats the stake until it glows and the chosen men drive it into the Cyclops's eye.
Odysseus twist it as blood and steam erupt.
Polyphemus wakes with a roar and tears it free.
Other Cyclopes call from outside, but leave when he says Nobody is killing him.
Polyphemus gropes at the entrance while the men hide among the animals.

title: Escape beneath the Rams
script: Scene ten. Escape beneath the Rams.
At dawn Polyphemus opens the cave and feels every animal's back as it passes.
Odysseus binds three rams abreast for each man, suspending a sailor beneath the middle animal.
Clings beneath the great lead ram while Polyphemus speaks tenderly to it.
Outside, the men release themselves, drive the flock to the ship, and row away.
Odysseus divide the animals and sacrifice the great ram to Zeus.

title: The Boast and the Curse
script: Scene eleven. The Boast and the Curse.
Hear me now, Polyphemus: the blinded Cyclops despite his men's pleas.
Polyphemus tears off a mountain peak and hurls it, driving a wave that nearly beaches the ship again.
That Odysseus return late, alone, and in pain?
A second rock misses as the ship escapes to the fleet.

title: Aeolus and the Bag of Winds
script: Book ten. The Bewitching Queen of Aeaea. Scene one. Aeolus and the Bag of Winds.
Gives a sealed oxhide bag containing every adverse wind and releases the west wind for Ithaca.
After nine days Ithaca appears, but Odysseus falls asleep at the helm.
The crew opens the bag, believing it contains treasure, and the winds blast them back to Aeolia.
No. I will not further aid, judging Odysseus hated by the gods.

title: The Laestrygonian Harbor
script: The fleet enters a narrow harbor ringed by cliffs.
The queen summons Antiphates, who seizes and eats one scout.
Laestrygonians mass on the cliffs, spear crews like fish, and crush the trapped ships with boulders.
Odysseus cuts his cable and escapes with only his own ship.

title: Scouts on Aeaea
script: The lone ship reaches Aeaea and the exhausted survivors rest for two days.
Odysseus climbs a lookout and sees smoke inland, then kills a great stag for food.
Odysseus divides the crew into two groups and draws lots.
Eurylochus leads twenty-two men toward Circe's house while Odysseus remains with the ship.

title: Circe Transforms the Crew
script: Scene four. Circe Transforms the Crew.
The scouts find Circe singing at her loom while enchanted wolves and lions fawn around them.
Circe serves drugged food and strikes them with her wand.
The men become pigs in body while retaining human minds.
Circe shuts them in pens and throws them acorns.

title: Hermes Gives the Moly
script: Scene five. Hermes Gives the Moly.
Odysseus arms himself and heads alone toward Circe's house despite Eurylochus's protest.
Pulls the black-rooted, white-flowered moly from the earth and gives it to Odysseus.
Resist the drug, draw your sword, and force Circe to swear an oath.

title: Odysseus Defeats Circe's Spell
script: Scene six. Odysseus Defeats Circe's Spell.
Circe serves Odysseus the drugged mixture and strikes him with her wand.
he draws his sword and rushes her.
Circe recognizes the foretold man, kneels, and offers her bed.
Odysseus requires the binding oath that she will not unman or harm him.
No. I will not eat while his crew remain imprisoned.

title: The Men Restored
script: Circe leads Odysseus to the pigsties and applies a second drug.
The swine regain human form, younger and more handsome than before.
Circe recognize Odysseus and embrace him in tears.
The men live in Circe's halls for a year until they demand the journey resume.

title: The Road to the Dead
script: Scene eight. The Road to the Dead.
Circe to honor your promise of homeward passage?
He must first consult Tiresias in the land of the dead.
Gives directions to Ocean's edge and the ritual for summoning spirits.
Elpenor, sleeping on the roof, wakes confused, falls, and dies unnoticed.
The crew launches in grief while Circe sends a favorable wind.

title: The Blood Pit Opens
script: Book eleven. The Kingdom of the Dead. Scene one. The Blood Pit Opens.
The ship reaches the misty land of the Cimmerians at Ocean's edge.
Odysseus digs a trench, pours libations, sacrifices sheep, and holds the spirits back with his sword.
The dead gather in multitudes, crying around the blood.
Odysseus waits for Tiresias before allowing any other shade to drink.

title: Elpenor Asks for Burial
script: Scene two. Elpenor Asks for Burial.
Elpenor's unburied ghost approaches first and Odysseus weeps in recognition.
His roof fall and begs for funeral rites on Aeaea.
That your oar be planted over the mound as a sign of your life?
I promise: to perform the burial after returning from the dead.

title: Tiresias Names the Cost
script: Scene three. Tiresias Names the Cost.
Tiresias drinks the blood and recognizes Odysseus.
Take warning: Poseidon pursues him for blinding Polyphemus.
Spare the Sun's cattle or face shipwreck and total loss.
Tiresias foretells Odysseus's lone return, the suitors' punishment, and a final inland journey carrying an oar.
After a distant sacrifice to Poseidon, death will come gently in old age.

title: Anticleia and the Three Embraces
script: Scene four. Anticleia and the Three Embraces.
Odysseus describes Penelope's fidelity, Telemachus's position, and Laertes's isolated grief.
Longing for I, not disease, caused her death.
Odysseus tries three times to embrace her, but his arms pass through the shade.

title: The Heroines of the Past
script: Scene five. The Heroines of the Past.
Odysseus lets a succession of famous women drink and identify their lineages.
Tyro tells of Poseidon and your river-born sons.
Antiope, Alcmene, Megara, Epicaste, Chloris, Leda, Iphimedeia, Phaedra, Ariadne, Maera, Clymene, and Eriphyle appear.
The sequence becomes a living genealogy of desire, birth, crime, and death.

title: Agamemnon's Warning
script: Agamemnon drinks and tells how Aegisthus and Clytemnestra murdered him at a feast.
He describes Cassandra's death and his wife's refusal even to close his eyes.
Take warning: Odysseus to return secretly and distrust women.
About Orestes, but Odysseus has no news?

title: Achilles Chooses Life in Retrospect
script: Scene seven. Achilles Chooses Life in Retrospect.
Achilles approaches with Patroclus, Antilochus, and Ajax nearby.
No. I will not death's glory.
Listen, and I will tell it in order. Neoptolemus's courage at Troy.
No. I will not reconciliation and withdraws in silence.

title: Judges, Punishments, and Flight
script: Scene eight. Judges, Punishments, and Flight.
Odysseus sees Minos judging the dead and Orion hunting shades of animals.
Odysseus sees Tityus attacked by vultures, Tantalus unable to drink or eat, and Sisyphus pushing his stone.
Speaks while the hero himself feasts among gods.
The dead crowd closer and Odysseus fears Persephone may send a monster.
Heracles's phantom retreats to the ship and sails back across Ocean.

title: Elpenor's Funeral
script: Book twelve. The Cattle of the Sun. Scene one. Elpenor's Funeral.
The ship returns to Aeaea and the exhausted crew sleeps on shore.
At dawn they retrieve Elpenor's body, burn it with his armor, and raise a mound.
They plant his oar at the top as promised.
Circe arrives with food, wine, and knowledge that they have returned from death.

title: Circe Maps the Dangers
script: Scene two. Circe Maps the Dangers.
The Sirens, Scylla, Charybdis, and Thrinacia.
Gives exact procedures for wax, binding, steering, sacrifice, and restraint.
This cannot stand: his appetite for combat.
At dawn the crew launches under a favorable wind.

title: The Sirens' Song
script: The wind dies as the ship approaches the Sirens' island.
Odysseus softens wax and seals every crewman's ears.
The men bind him upright to the mast and row past the flowered shore.
Odysseus struggles and signals to be released.
Perimedes and Eurylochus tighten the ropes until the song fades.

title: Between Scylla and Charybdis
script: Scene four. Between Scylla and Charybdis.
The crew hears Charybdis roar and sees spray rising from the whirlpool.
Odysseus arms himself despite Circe's warning and searches the rock face.
Scylla's six heads strike, lifting six screaming men from the ship.
The survivors pass beyond both monsters while watching their companions die above them.

title: The Island of the Sun
script: Scene five. The Island of the Sun.
The exhausted crew sees the cattle and sheep of Helios on Thrinacia.
Sail past, but Eurylochus accuses him of mercilessness.
The men swear to touch no livestock and land for one night.
A month of storm winds traps them while stores diminish.
Odysseus repeatedly reminds them of the oath.

title: The Cattle Are Slaughtered
script: Scene six. The Cattle Are Slaughtered.
When food is gone, Odysseus withdraws inland to pray and the gods put him to sleep.
Eurylochus persuades the crew to sacrifice the best cattle rather than starve.
Eurylochus substitute oak leaves for barley and water for wine, kill the animals, and roast the meat.
The hides crawl and the meat bellows on the spits.
Lampetie tells Helios, who demands punishment from Zeus.

title: Zeus Destroys the Last Ship
script: Scene seven. Zeus Destroys the Last Ship.
This cannot stand: the act, but the crew feasts for six days.
On the seventh day the wind falls and the ship leaves Thrinacia.
Zeus gathers a black cloud and strikes the mast with lightning.
The ship shatters and every crewman drowns.
Odysseus lashes keel and mast together.
Driven back to Charybdis, he hangs from the fig tree until the timbers reemerge, then drifts alone to Calypso.

title: The Phaeacians Carry Odysseus Home
script: Book thirteen. Ithaca at Last. Scene one. The Phaeacians Carry Odysseus Home.
Odysseus finishes his tale and the Phaeacians sit in silence.
Additional gifts packed in a chest and the farewell feast begins.
At sunset Odysseus boards the convoy ship and lies on a prepared bed in the stern.
The ship runs faster than a hawk while he sleeps and reaches Ithaca before dawn.
The crew carries the sleeping man and his treasure onto the shore.

title: Odysseus Wakes on an Unknown Shore
script: Scene two. Odysseus Wakes on an Unknown Shore.
What shore is this? The ship is gone, and even the land has hidden its face from me.
The gifts are all here. Then they did not rob me, but where have they left me?
Give me one true sign, a harbor, a hill, a name I can believe.
Stranger, why do you wander this coast with treasure at your feet and fear in your eyes?

title: The Cretan Lie Meets Its Match
script: Scene three. The Cretan Lie Meets Its Match.
The shepherd tells Odysseus you is in Ithaca and the hero suppresses your joy.
He invents a Cretan identity and a story of killing a king's son and fleeing by Phoenician ship.
How long must this endure? that she abandoned him after Troy.
Poseidon's anger required concealment rather than open rescue.

title: The Treasure Is Hidden
script: Scene four. The Treasure Is Hidden.
Athena helps Odysseus carry the gifts into the cave of the nymphs.
Athena seals the cave entrance with a stone and sits with him beneath the olive tree.
Athena count the suitors and devise a concealment strategy.
Take the next step: Go first to Eumaeus while you retrieves Telemachus from Sparta.

title: Athena Makes the Beggar
script: Scene five. Athena Makes the Beggar.
Athena touches Odysseus with her wand and shrivels his skin, hair, and limbs.
Clouds his eyes, dresses him in filthy rags, and gives him a staff and patched bag.
The transformed king is instructed to test servants without being recognized.
Athena departs for Sparta and Odysseus walks toward Eumaeus's farm.

title: The Dogs at Eumaeus's Yard
script: Book fourteen. The Loyal Swineherd. Scene one. The Dogs at Eumaeus's Yard.
Odysseus approaches Eumaeus's remote pig farm in disguise.
Four savage dogs rush him and he drops his staff and sits to avoid attack.
Eumaeus runs out, scatters the dogs with stones, and brings the stranger inside.
Eumaeus offers his own seat and prepares two young pigs for a meal.

title: The Swineherd Laments His Master
script: Scene two. The Swineherd Laments His Master.
Eumaeus apologizes for the humble food and curses the suitors who consume Odysseus's best animals.
Speaks of the absent king with loyalty and refuses to believe hopeful travelers' stories.
I swear: the master will return within the year.
No. I will not he prediction but continues to honor the stranger.

title: The Cretan Tale at the Hut
script: Scene three. The Cretan Tale at the Hut.
At Eumaeus's request the beggar invents a long life as a Cretan warrior and raider.
Tells of Troy, a disastrous Egyptian raid, enslavement, escape, and a Thesprotian report of Odysseus.
The tale mixes precise truth with false identity and tests what Eumaeus will accept.
No. I will not he claim that Odysseus is near.

title: The Cloak Test
script: Night turns cold and wet as Eumaeus's herdsmen return.
Mark the order. Tells a story of tricking I into obtaining a cloak during the war.
Eumaeus understands the indirect request and lends the stranger a heavy cloak.
Eumaeus sleeps near the pigs himself, guarding the herd through the storm.

bookTitle: The Prince Sets Sail for Home
title: Athena Wakes Telemachus
script: Book fifteen. The Prince Sets Sail for Home. Scene one. Athena Wakes Telemachus.
Do not drift from the course. You in Sparta and orders him to return before Penelope is forced to marry.
Take warning: the suitors wait in ambush and gives a route that avoids the strait.
Take the next step: Land secretly and go first to Eumaeus's hut.
Telemachus wakes Pisistratus and prepares to depart at dawn.

bookTitle: The Prince Sets Sail for Home
title: Farewell from Menelaus and Helen
script: Scene two. Farewell from Menelaus and Helen.
And Pisistratus take leave of Menelaus after the king insists on gifts and a final meal.
Gives a robe and reads a bird omen as Odysseus's imminent revenge.
The chariot travels back through Phera to Pylos.
Pisistratus to take him directly to the ship so Nestor cannot delay him with hospitality?

bookTitle: The Prince Sets Sail for Home
title: Theoclymenus Joins the Voyage
script: Scene three. Theoclymenus Joins the Voyage.
For passage after killing a kinsman?
The ship leaves under Athena's wind and sails through the night toward Ithaca.

bookTitle: The Prince Sets Sail for Home
title: Eumaeus Tells His Own Story
script: Scene four. Eumaeus Tells His Own Story.
No. I will not expose him to the suitors.
About Laertes, Anticleia, and Eumaeus's origins?
Tells how Phoenician traders abducted him from the island of Syria after corrupting a slave woman.
Laertes bought him in Ithaca and the royal household raised him.

bookTitle: The Prince Sets Sail for Home
title: Telemachus Lands in Secret
script: Scene five. Telemachus Lands in Secret.
As the ship approaches Ithaca, a hawk tears a dove beside Telemachus.
Theoclymenus reads the omen as proof that Odysseus's line will remain supreme.
Take the ship to town while you lands near Eumaeus's farm.
Telemachus entrusts Theoclymenus to Piraeus and walks inland alone.

title: The Son Reaches the Hut
script: Book sixteen. Father and Son. Scene one. The Son Reaches the Hut.
Telemachus approaches Eumaeus's farm and the dogs greet him without aggression.
Eumaeus recognizes him, drops his bowl, and kisses him like a father receiving a lost son.
The disguised Odysseus rises and offers his seat.
For news and enters the hut beside the unknown beggar?

title: Eumaeus Carries News to Penelope
script: Scene two. Eumaeus Carries News to Penelope.
Eumaeus to report your safe return to Penelope privately?
Eumaeus leaves for town, taking the farm-to-palace road.
Athena appears outside the hut, visible only to Odysseus, and signals that recognition may begin.
Odysseus follows her outside while Telemachus remains within.

title: The Father Reveals Himself
script: Scene three. The Father Reveals Himself.
Athena restores Odysseus's strength, clothing, skin, and dark hair outside the hut.
Telemachus recoils, believing he is a god.
Himself the father for whom Telemachus has suffered.
Telemachus embrace and weep with the force of birds robbed of their young.

title: The Plan against the Suitors
script: Scene four. The Plan against the Suitors.
For the exact number of suitors?
Take warning: two men cannot fight so many.
Names Zeus and Athena as allies and lays out the weapons-removal plan.
Telemachus must return to the palace, endure insults, and tell no one, not even Penelope or Laertes.
Telemachus assign Eumaeus to bring the beggar later.

title: The Ambush Fails and the Suitors Divide
script: Scene five. The Ambush Fails and the Suitors Divide.
Telemachus's ship reaches harbor before the ambush vessel can intercept it.
A herald publicly announces the prince's return before Eumaeus can deliver the private message.
Argues they must seek a favorable omen first.

title: The Beggar Returns
script: Athena changes Odysseus back into the old beggar before Eumaeus returns.
Telemachus's safe arrival and the suitors' failed ship.
A messenger from the crew reaches Penelope with the same news.
The three men eat and sleep while father and son preserve the secret.

title: Telemachus Returns to the Palace
script: Book seventeen. Stranger at the Gates. Scene one. Telemachus Returns to the Palace.
Eurycleia and Penelope embrace him in tears.
What Nestor and Menelaus told him but withholds the plan and his father's return.
Odysseus is already in Ithaca, preparing revenge.

title: The Road with Melanthius
script: Scene two. The Road with Melanthius.
Eumaeus leads the disguised Odysseus from the farm toward town.
At a fountain they meet Melanthius driving the suitors' best goats.
Is that the best you can offer, Eumaeus?
Odysseus suppresses the urge to kill him and continues toward the palace.

title: Argos Recognizes His Master
script: Scene three. Argos Recognizes His Master.
Near the palace Odysseus sees his old dog Argos lying neglected on dung.
Argos lifts his head, drops his ears, and wags his tail at the scent and voice of his master.
Odysseus turns aside to hide a tear while asking Eumaeus about the animal.
After twenty years Argos dies as soon as he has recognized Odysseus.

title: The Beggar Enters His Hall
script: Scene four. The Beggar Enters His Hall.
Eumaeus enters first and Telemachus signals him to seat the beggar at the door.
Odysseus crosses his own threshold unrecognized and hears Phemius singing.
By whatever you hold sacred, hear me: from suitor to suitor to test each man's character.
Most give food while Antinous demands to know who admitted him.

title: Antinous Throws the Stool
script: Scene five. Antinous Throws the Stool.
Antinous hurls a footstool into his shoulder.
Even the other suitors condemn the violation of a stranger.

title: Penelope Summons the Stranger
script: Scene six. Penelope Summons the Stranger.
Do not mistake my silence. Eumaeus to bring him for questioning?
Odysseus delays until dusk, saying the suitors may attack him in the open hall.
Do not mistake my silence. When the room empties?
Penelope reads it as an omen that the suitors will die.

title: Eumaeus Leaves the Hall
script: Scene seven. Eumaeus Leaves the Hall.
Come back at dawn with news.
Eumaeus takes leave of the disguised Odysseus and the prince without recognizing their bond.
The beggar remains in the palace under the suitors' gaze.

title: Irus Challenges the Stranger
script: Book eighteen. The Beggar-King of Ithaca. Scene one. Irus Challenges the Stranger.
Move away from this threshold, old man, before I drag you out by the ankle. There is room for only one beggar here.
I have done you no harm. Take your share and leave mine alone, or you may learn how little age tells you about a man’s hands.
Fight for the threshold. The winner eats with us; the loser is thrown out where no one will hear him complain.
Swear that none of you will strike me while I face him. Let the contest belong to the two men who entered it.

title: Odysseus Drops Irus
script: Irus trembles but is forced into the ring.
Odysseus chooses not to kill him and breaks his jaw with one compact blow.
Mark the order. Take warning: him not to return.
Cheer and Amphinomus gives the victor food and wine.

title: The Warning to Amphinomus
script: Scene three. The Warning to Amphinomus.
Take warning: no man should become lawless in prosperity.
Hear what will come: I will return before the suitor can leave the palace.
Amphinomus walks away shaken, sensing danger but unable to escape Athena's design.
The warning becomes another unheeded exit offered before the slaughter.

title: Penelope Appears before the Suitors
script: Scene four. Penelope Appears before the Suitors.
Athena places a desire in Penelope to appear before the suitors and inflame their gifts.
Athena puts the queen to sleep, beautifies her, and wakes her radiant.
Penelope descends with two maids and rebukes Telemachus for allowing the stranger's abuse.
Listen, and I will tell it in order. Odysseus's parting instructions and demands courtship gifts.
The suitors send for jewels, robes, and ornaments while Odysseus silently rejoices at her strategy.

title: Melantho and Eurymachus Attack
script: Scene five. Melantho and Eurymachus Attack.
After Penelope withdraws, disloyal maids light the hall for the suitors.
Take warning: the master may return.
Is that the best you can offer, the beggar's baldness and offers him labor only to belittle him?
With a challenge of work and war.
Eurymachus throws a stool and misses.
Telemachus rebukes the suitors and ends the night's disorder.

title: The Weapons Leave the Hall
script: Book nineteen. Penelope and Her Guest. Scene one. The Weapons Leave the Hall.
Remove the weapons from the hall.
Athena carries a golden lamp while father and son take shields, spears, and helmets to the storeroom.
Tells Eurycleia the smoke has damaged them and you must be protected from drunken quarrels.
The hall is left apparently defenseless for the future contest.

title: Penelope Begins the Test
script: Scene two. Penelope Begins the Test.
The hearth and orders Melantho to stop insulting the guest.
Do not mistake my silence. Who you is, but you resists naming your lineage before hearing your grief?
Penelope describes the suitors and the shroud deception.
Do not mistake my silence. For proof that the stranger truly knows Odysseus?

title: The Stranger Describes Odysseus
script: Scene three. The Stranger Describes Odysseus.
Odysseus invents the Cretan name Aethon and claims to have hosted Odysseus before Troy.
Odysseus describes the king's purple cloak, golden brooch, tunic, and herald Eurybates in exact detail.
Penelope weeps as if melting snow while Odysseus keeps his eyes hard despite inward grief.
The stranger truly encountered her husband.
I swear: swears Odysseus is near and will return within the month.

title: Eurycleia Finds the Scar
script: Scene four. Eurycleia Finds the Scar.
Wash the stranger's feet because your age resembles Odysseus's.
Odysseus recognizes the danger but cannot refuse without suspicion.
The nurse touches the old boar scar and instantly knows him.
Odysseus drops the foot into the basin, spilling water, and reaches toward Penelope.
Odysseus grips her throat gently but firmly and makes her swear silence.

title: The Boar Hunt on Parnassus
script: Scene five. The Boar Hunt on Parnassus.
The scar triggers the story of young Odysseus visiting his grandfather Autolycus.
At dawn he hunts with his uncles on Mount Parnassus.
A boar bursts from dense cover and charges.
Odysseus spears it but receives a deep tusk wound above the knee.
The hunters bind the wound, stop the blood with a charm, and carry him home.

title: The Dream of the Geese
script: Scene six. The Dream of the Geese.
After the secret is restored, I tells the beggar your dream of twenty geese killed by a great eagle.
In the dream the eagle speaks with Odysseus's voice and says the geese are the suitors.
Insists the dream has one unavoidable meaning.
Announces the bow contest: she will marry the man who strings Odysseus's bow and shoots through twelve axes.
Withdraws upstairs and Athena gives her sleep.

title: The Restless Night
script: Book twenty. Portents Gather. Scene one. The Restless Night.
Odysseus lies awake in the portico, angered by disloyal maids slipping out to the suitors.
Why you doubts after reaching home?
I promise: protection even against many enemies and gives him sleep.
Hear me, for death, and dreams that Odysseus lies beside her.

title: Thunder and the Mill Woman
script: Scene two. Thunder and the Mill Woman.
Zeus for a double sign from sky and household?
Zeus thunders from a clear sky.
Hear me, that the suitors' next feast be their last.
Odysseus recognizes both signs and takes courage.

title: The Herdsmen Arrive
script: Eurycleia wakes the household and servants prepare the hall for Apollo's feast day.
Welcome. Come inside, take food, and speak when you are ready.
Melanthius enters with goats and renews his abuse.
Philoetius brings cattle, takes the stranger's hand, and weeps because he resembles Odysseus.
Hear what will come: predicts the master's return before the herdsman leaves.

title: The Ox Hoof
script: No. I will not immediate action.
Is that the best you can offer, the beggar and hurls an ox hoof as a guest-gift?
Continue, and to spear the offender if another assault occurs.
No. I will not control her choice.

title: The Hall of Death
script: Scene five. The Hall of Death.
Athena drives the suitors into uncontrollable laughter while their meat drips blood in their vision.
Their faces distort and tears run beneath the laughter.
Theoclymenus sees darkness covering them, ghosts crowding the court, and blood on the walls.
Announces their approaching destruction and leaves when they mock him.
Telemachus and Odysseus watch one another across the doomed feast.

title: Penelope Retrieves the Bow
script: Book twenty-one. Odysseus Strings His Bow. Scene one. Penelope Retrieves the Bow.
Athena inspires Penelope to begin the contest that will expose the suitors to slaughter.
The queen enters the storeroom, unlocks the doors, and lifts Odysseus's bow and quiver down.
Athena sits with the weapon across her knees and weeps before carrying it to the hall.
Two maids bring the chest of axes and set the implements before the suitors.

title: The Contest Is Set
script: Scene two. The Contest Is Set.
She will marry whoever strings the bow and shoots through all twelve axes.
Eumaeus and Philoetius weep at the sight of their master's weapon.
Telemachus plants the axes in a straight line and tries the bow three times.
On the fourth attempt he nearly strings it, but Odysseus signals him to stop.

title: The Suitors Fail the Bow
script: Scene three. The Suitors Fail the Bow.
Hear what will come: tries first, cannot bend the bow, and predicts it will destroy many suitors.
One after another the men strain, sweat, and fail.
Melanthius lights a fire and brings fat so the bow can be warmed and greased.
Even Eurymachus cannot string it and suffers humiliation.
Antinous postpones the contest for Apollo's festival feast.

title: Odysseus Recruits the Herdsmen
script: Scene four. Odysseus Recruits the Herdsmen.
Odysseus follows Eumaeus and Philoetius outside and tests their loyalty.
The herdsmen embrace him and weep, then swear support.
Assigns Eumaeus to deliver the bow, Philoetius to lock the courtyard gate, and both to secure the women.

title: The Beggar Requests the Bow
script: Scene five. The Beggar Requests the Bow.
To test your strength with the bow?
The suitors erupt in anger and fear that a beggar may succeed.
Insists the stranger deserves a try and promises clothing and weapons if he wins.
Eumaeus carries the bow through the shouting crowd to Odysseus.

title: The Doors Are Secured
script: Scene six. The Doors Are Secured.
Eurycleia locks the women into their quarters at Telemachus's instruction.
Philoetius fastens the courtyard gate with a ship's cable.
Odysseus turns the bow in his hands, inspecting every part while the suitors mock him.
The hidden allies take their assigned positions and the escape routes close.

title: The Bow Sings
script: Odysseus strings the bow effortlessly, as a musician strings a lyre.
Telemachus places sword and spear beside him and moves to his father's side.
Odysseus nocks an arrow and shoots cleanly through all twelve axes.
Tells you that the stranger has not disgraced the house and signals the next phase.

title: Antinous Falls
script: Book twenty-two. Slaughter in the Hall. Scene one. Antinous Falls.
Odysseus strips off his rags, leaps onto the threshold, and pours the remaining arrows before him.
Odysseus shoots Antinous through the throat while the suitor lifts a cup.
Antinous falls across the table, spilling food and wine as the room erupts.
The suitors assume an accident and search for weapons that are no longer there.
Names himself and accuses them of consuming his house and violating his servants.

title: Eurymachus Bargains and Attacks
script: Scene two. Eurymachus Bargains and Attacks.
Eurymachus blames Antinous and offers repayment many times over if Odysseus spares them.
I promise: no survivor can escape his rage.
Eurymachus rallies the suitors to rush the archer beneath raised tables.
Odysseus shoots Eurymachus in the chest.
Amphinomus charges and Telemachus kills him with a spear.

title: The Storeroom Arms the Defenders
script: Scene three. The Storeroom Arms the Defenders.
Telemachus runs to the storeroom and brings shields, helmets, and spears for Odysseus, Eumaeus, Philoetius, and himself.
Telemachus admits leaving the door unbarred after one trip.
The defenders arm in formation while Odysseus continues firing.
When the arrows run low they transition to spear combat.

title: Melanthius Arms the Suitors
script: Scene four. Melanthius Arms the Suitors.
Melanthius discovers the open storeroom route and carries weapons to the suitors.
Odysseus catch Melanthius returning for more arms.
Odysseus bind his hands and feet, hoist him by a rope to the rafters, and leave him suspended in pain.

title: Athena Tests the Battle
script: Scene five. Athena Tests the Battle.
Come then. your for delaying aid.
Odysseus rebukes him but first tests his strength by remaining disguised and partially withholding help.
Athena deflects them into walls and doors.
The defenders answer with a coordinated volley and kill several men.
Athena raises her aegis from the roof beam and terror breaks the remaining formation.

title: The Hall Is Cleared
script: Scene six. The Hall Is Cleared.
Odysseus and his allies pursue the suitors through the hall like falcons among smaller birds.
Leiodes clasps Odysseus's knees but is killed despite claiming innocence.
Phemius and Medon appeal for mercy and Telemachus confirms their limited complicity.
Mark the order. Them into the courtyard.
The living search the blood-filled hall for any remaining threat.

title: The Disloyal Maids
script: Identifies twelve maids who consorted with the suitors and mocked the household.
The women are forced to carry bodies outside and clean the hall with water and sponges.
No. I will not a clean sword death and hangs them together from a cable in the courtyard.
Melanthius is lowered, mutilated, and killed.
The household's corrupted labor system is violently purged.

title: The House Calls Penelope
script: Scene eight. The House Calls Penelope.
Bring sulfur and fire so the hall can be purified.
Loyal women enter, recognize him, and embrace him in tears.
Odysseus receives them while restraining grief and maintaining security.
Odysseus sends Eurycleia upstairs to wake Penelope and announce that her husband has returned.

title: Eurycleia Wakes Penelope
script: Book twenty-three. The Great Rooted Bed. Scene one. Eurycleia Wakes Penelope.
Wakes Penelope and says Odysseus has returned and killed the suitors.
Penelope first thinks the nurse has gone mad or that a god punished the men.
Eurycleia offers the scar as proof and describes the king waiting below.
Penelope descends, divided between embracing him and testing him from a distance.

title: Penelope Studies the Stranger
script: Scene two. Penelope Studies the Stranger.
She and Odysseus share private signs.
The delay and turns to the danger from the suitors' families.
Create the sound of a wedding so the deaths remain hidden.

title: The False Wedding Noise
script: Scene three. The False Wedding Noise.
Odysseus bathes while Athena restores his stature and beauty.
Phemius plays the lyre and the household dances so neighbors believe a wedding is underway.
No. I will not immediate recognition.
You are the cause of this: your heart of being harder than stone.

title: The Bed Test
script: Move the marriage bed outside the chamber for the stranger.
Odysseus erupts, explaining that he built the bed around a living olive tree and no one could move it intact.
Penelope runs to him and embraces him.
Fear of deception caused her delay.
Athena holds back dawn while husband and wife weep and reunite.

title: Odysseus Tells the Remaining Journey
script: Scene five. Odysseus Tells the Remaining Journey.
In bed Odysseus and Penelope recount the years they spent apart.
Travel inland with an oar and appease Poseidon.
Odysseus describes the eventual gentle death foretold for him.
Further movement remains even after homecoming.
Penelope sleep while Athena finally releases the dawn.

title: Departure for Laertes
script: At dawn Odysseus arms himself with Telemachus, Eumaeus, and Philoetius.
Mark the order. Remain inside and reveal nothing.
Athena covers the four men in darkness as they leave the city.
Athena travel toward Laertes's farm before the suitors' deaths become public.

title: The Suitors Enter Hades
script: Book twenty-four. Peace. Scene one. The Suitors Enter Hades.
Hermes gathers the suitors' shades with his wand and leads them squeaking like bats toward the dead.
Hermes pass Ocean, the White Rock, the Gates of the Sun, and the land of dreams.
In the meadow of asphodel they meet Achilles, Agamemnon, Ajax, and other warriors.
The dead gather to hear how so many noble young men died together.

title: Agamemnon Hears of Penelope's Fidelity
script: Scene two. Agamemnon Hears of Penelope's Fidelity.
Agamemnon and Achilles debate the honor of their deaths and funerals.
Amphimedon tells how Penelope delayed the suitors, how Odysseus returned as a beggar, and how the bow contest became slaughter.
This cannot stand: Clytemnestra by contrast.
The underworld recognizes Odysseus's household victory as a new song.

title: Odysseus Tests Laertes
script: Odysseus reaches the farm and finds Laertes alone in patched clothes, tending a tree.
Odysseus sends his companions to prepare food and approaches under another false identity.
Odysseus claims to have hosted Odysseus years earlier and watches his father collapse in grief.
Unable to continue, I embraces him and names himself.

title: The Scar and the Orchard Trees
script: Scene four. The Scar and the Orchard Trees.
Odysseus shows the boar scar as physical proof.
Names the thirteen pear trees, ten apple trees, forty fig trees, and fifty vine rows Laertes gave him as a child.
Laertes recognizes the private map of inheritance and collapses into his son's arms.
Laertes fears that Ithaca lacks men willing to defend them from the suitors' kin.

title: Laertes Is Restored
script: Laertes is bathed and anointed inside the farmhouse.
Athena makes him taller and stronger, restoring royal presence.
Dolius and his sons return from the fields, recognize Odysseus, and join the feast.
The reunited household eats while rumors of the massacre spread through town.

title: The Families Demand Revenge
script: Scene six. The Families Demand Revenge.
How long must this endure? In town the bodies are carried from the palace and each family mourns its dead.
Medon and Phemius testify that a god fought beside Odysseus.
Halitherses reminds the people that he warned them and that their own tolerance enabled the disaster.
No. I will not caution and leads armed relatives toward Laertes's farm.
Some citizens refuse to join and remain behind.

title: Zeus and Athena Set the Terms
script: Scene seven. Zeus and Athena Set the Terms.
Whether the conflict should continue or peace should be imposed?
Odysseus may remain king after punishing the suitors.
Forget the bloodshed through oath and renewed prosperity.
Athena descends toward Ithaca to terminate the cycle.

title: The Last Clash
script: Odysseus sees the armed relatives approaching and distributes weapons among the farm household.
Do not drift from the course. Prove its strength.
Hear me, prays, throws a spear, and kills Eupithes through the helmet.
Odysseus and Telemachus charge the remaining attackers.
The final battle begins to repeat the slaughter that peace must stop.

title: Athena Makes Peace
script: Listen closely. Stop and tells the Ithacans to disperse without more blood.
Zeus hurls a thunderbolt before her feet, making the command irresistible.
Odysseus establishes binding oaths between king and people in Mentor's form.
The poem ends with the household restored and the violence converted into civic peace.
